description.narrative: In Vietnam, including Hue City, the default family care work belongs to women, men rarely share these tasks. The target audience inthis project is women who work as low-income, precarious bottle workers, in addition to having to do all the work of taking care ofthe family. So through this project, we want to change the perception and behavior of the community, men will share housework with women, women will have more voice in the family. "Balancing work and family, it's not going to be a saying just for women anymore but for men as well." • What will have changed as a direct result of this initiative: - Women who work as bottlers will have less burden of housework, more time to rest, take care of themselves and participate in social activities - Changing the perceptions and behaviors of other family members, especially men, who actively share household chores with women - Changing society's perception of family care tasks, not just a woman's job but that of all family members. * Key project activities: - Research policies on gender equality in Vietnam in general and Hue in particular. - FPAR [10 sessions] - An Dong ward: + Formation of the group: 10 women working as bottlers. - Communication campaign: build a typical story, tell the story to the community on social networks - Establish a husband-and-wife club: men share housework with women in the family. - Survey: about sharing family care work in Hue city (number of 100 votes) - Evaluation of project results (preliminary)

participating-org.narrative: Centre for Social Research and Development (CSRD) is a local non-government organization which is registered with the Hue Union of Science and Technology Associations (HUSTA). CSRD has been registered and operated since 2008. CSRD is based in Hue in the Central Region of Vietnam, and many of the projects have been located in the provinces of Central Region. CSRD also works throughout Vietnam and more broadly in South East Asia on water resources issues because CSRD is the administration centre for the Vietnam Rivers Network (VRN). The CSRD mission is to work towards a better life for all people in Vietnam, particularly for those who are poor and vulnerable, and adversely impacted by Vietnam#s industrial development. The hydropower industry is a current focus because many power plants are planned and many are already operating. CSRD#s approach is to work in partnership with local communities and grass roots groups, and to bring communities together so that they may learn from each other. The organization#s work has been recognized by local and provincial authorities and by the National Union of Science and Technology Associations. CSRD maintains very good relationships with community partners; and has a positive record for achieving specific project outcomes.
